title: She Kissed Me Much, as if She Feared
text:
She kissed me much, as if she feared

leaving very early... Her affection was

restless, nervous. I did not understand

such feverish haste. My coarse intention

never saw very far.

She sensed it!

She sensed that the term was short,

that the sail wounded by the lash

of the wind was already waiting..., and in her anxiety

she wanted to leave me her soul in every embrace,

to place an eternity in her kisses.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the belated understanding of urgent kisses before death.

title: Whoever Knows He Is One with God, Attains Nirvana...
text:
Whoever knows he is one with God attains Nirvana:

a Nirvana in which every darkness is illumined;

vertiginous widening of human consciousness,

which is only a projection of the Divine Idea

in Time...


The phenomenon, the exterior, vain fruit

of illusion, is extinguished: there is no longer plurality,

and the I, ecstatic, at last plunges into the absolute,

and has all eternity as inheritance!
editorial_note: This first-line version preserves the same metaphysical argument from illusion to unity.

title: Alchemy
text:
I know well that to see you

I need the alchemy of death

that will transmute me into soul, and delirious

with love and anxiety, each instant

that arrives, I require it

saying to it: "Ah, if you were the last!"


So measureless, so divine

and so deep is the future I divine

through the stellar routes,

and from one to another of the avatars,

always with you, noble companion,

that to be able to die, ah, what would I not give!
editorial_note: The translation keeps death as the alchemy needed for reunion across avatars.

title: Kalpa
text:
In all the eternities

that preceded our world,

how can one deny that there already existed

planets with humanities;


and there were Homers who described

the first heroic deeds,

and there were Shakespeares who knew how to deepen

into the depths of the soul?


Serpent that bites your tail,

inflexible circle, black

ball that turns without cease,

monotonous refrain of the same

song, tide of the abyss,

are you a never-ending tale?...
editorial_note: The translation keeps cosmic recurrence as a serpent-circle and endless tale.

title: A Flower on the Road
text:
The dead woman rises again when I lean into your love,

I find her in your immense and tranquil gazes,

and in all of you... You both are as alike as

your face, which is copied twice in my pupils.

It is true: that one loved the radiant night,

and you always pleased your dream in dawns.

(That is why she was more lily, that is why you are more rose.)

It is true, that one spoke; you live silent,

and that one was paler; but you are sadder.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the comparison between the dead beloved and the living beloved.

title: Azrael
text:
Azrael, open your black and deep wing,

may its measureless canopy shelter me,

and beneath its beneficent refuge may hide

the incurable sadness of my life.


Azrael, biblical angel, strong angel,

angel of redemption, somber angel,

it is time for you to consecrate to death

my lightless brain: empty altar...


Azrael, my hope is an invalid;

my faith is now setting; dusk has come,

come, now it is necessary that I sleep...

To die..., to sleep..., to sleep...? To dream perhaps!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Hamlet echo at the close while preserving Azrael's devotional address.
